title: Mathematics — notable recent papers, week ending 2026-11-20
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart. The ordering is inferred, not a readership or download ranking; citation and independent-attention evidence is too sparse for this very recent batch, so this is a notable recent-paper selection rather than a measured list of the hottest papers.

sections.title: Thouless's bandwidth conjecture: a proof by elliptic periods
sections.abstract: For the critical rational Harper operator, the authors prove that the denominator times the total spectral bandwidth tends uniformly in the reduced numerator to 32G/π, with G Catalan’s constant.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove Thouless’s bandwidth asymptotic: for coprime 1≤p<q, q|S_{p,q}| tends uniformly in p to 32G/π as q→∞, where S_{p,q} is the union of the spectra over phase and G is Catalan’s constant (arXiv abstract and Theorem 1.1).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The critical Harper operator with rational parameter p/q, standard normalization, and total bandwidth defined as the measure of the union of spectra over all phases; uniformity is over reduced numerators.
sections.unique_caveat: This concerns the critical rational model and its total bandwidth, not individual spectral gaps or off-critical operators.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract states a sharp, explicit uniform asymptotic for a named conjecture and connects spectral theory to genus-one periods; the arXiv record cross-lists mathematical physics and spectral theory.

sections.title: The Borel Ruziewicz problem
sections.abstract: The authors prove uniqueness of rotation-invariant finitely additive probability measures on Borel subsets of spheres and normalized invariant finitely additive measure on bounded Borel subsets of Euclidean spaces in the stated dimensions, using finite rotation sets with spectral gap.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish the Borel Ruziewicz theorem: normalized surface measure is the only rotation-invariant finitely additive probability measure on Borel subsets of S^n for n≥2, and Lebesgue measure is the only normalized finitely additive measure on bounded Borel subsets of R^d invariant under orientation-preserving isometries for d≥3 (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Borel sets; sphere dimension n≥2 or Euclidean dimension d≥3; invariance can be reduced to finite sets of rotations with spectral gap (on R^d, two such sets about distinct centers).
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is explicitly for Borel-domain measures and the stated dimensions. The arXiv comments disclose that the main results were obtained by AI (hexagon:2611.00309v1), so independent expert verification is especially important.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A single theorem treats both spherical and Euclidean settings and gives a finite-generator spectral-gap criterion; the arXiv record cross-lists dynamics, functional analysis, and logic.

sections.title: A Poisson boundary solution to Connes' bicentralizer conjecture and Kadison's problem on MASA
sections.abstract: The author develops Poisson-boundary methods to prove a weak Dixmier property for inclusions with expectation, yielding new proofs of Connes’ and the relative bicentralizer conjectures and a conditional solution to Kadison’s MASA problem.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves that for a countably decomposable inclusion M⊂P with a normal faithful conditional expectation, M⊂c(P) has the weak Dixmier property; by cited characterizations this implies Connes’ and the relative bicentralizer conjectures, and under extra hypotheses yields a MASA of M that is also maximal abelian in P (arXiv abstract and Theorem A).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Countably decomposable von Neumann algebras with a normal faithful conditional expectation; the MASA conclusion additionally assumes separable preduals and M′∩P=Z(M).
sections.unique_caveat: This is an independent new proof of Connes’ conjecture after a recent proof already appeared; the Kadison-problem conclusion has the additional relative-commutant and separability hypotheses.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract reports a new proof route for a major conjecture plus the relative version and a second application to Kadison’s problem; categories span operator algebras and dynamics.

sections.title: A Proof of Stein's Equidissection Conjecture
sections.abstract: The author resolves Stein’s conjecture by proving that a balanced polygon cannot be dissected into an odd number of equal-area triangles.
sections.claimed_result: The author states that Stein’s conjecture holds in full: no balanced polygon admits an equidissection into an odd number of triangles (arXiv abstract and Conjecture 1 in the introduction).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A balanced polygon, meaning its oriented boundary segments can be paired into opposite vectors; an equidissection is a dissection into equal-area triangles.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is about balanced polygons and odd equidissections, not arbitrary polygons or arbitrary dissections.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The arXiv introduction says the full result removes the rational-vertex restriction of the previously known case; the paper is cross-listed in combinatorics and number theory.

sections.title: A disproof of the van Emde Boas--Kruyswijk conjecture on the Davenport constant
sections.abstract: The authors disprove the van Emde Boas–Kruyswijk formula for the Davenport constant by showing D(C_6^r)>5r+1 for every r≥23.
sections.claimed_result: The authors give a counterexample to the conjectured identity D(C_n^r)=r(n−1)+1, proving D(C_6^r)>5r+1 for every r≥23 (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: D(G) is the least length forcing a nontrivial zero-sum subsequence in every sequence from a finite abelian group G; the counterexample family is C_6^r for r≥23.
sections.unique_caveat: This refutes the proposed universal formula on one explicit family; it does not determine D(C_n^r) in general.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract gives a concrete disproof of a conjecture dating to 1969, with an explicit parameter range, and the record cross-lists combinatorics and number theory.

sections.title: Proof of the polygonal Saint-Venant inequality conjectured by Pólya--Szegö
sections.abstract: The authors prove that among polygons of prescribed area with at most n sides, the regular n-gon uniquely maximizes torsional rigidity, including when competitors are non-convex.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove the polygonal Saint-Venant inequality conjectured by Pólya–Szegö: for every n≥3, the regular n-gon uniquely maximizes torsional rigidity among possibly non-convex polygons of fixed area with at most n sides (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Planar polygons with prescribed area and at most n≥3 sides; competitors may be non-convex; objective is torsional rigidity.
sections.unique_caveat: The optimization class is polygons with a fixed side-count bound, not all planar domains.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract states a unique optimizer for every n and includes non-convex polygons, turning a conjectured inequality into a complete finite-side-class result.

sections.title: The Bessis Moussa Villani conjecture in finite von Neumann algebras
sections.abstract: The authors extend the Bessis–Moussa–Villani conjecture from matrix algebras to bounded operators in finite von Neumann algebras with faithful normal trace.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove the BMV conjecture for bounded operators in a finite von Neumann algebra with a faithful normal tracial state, constructing a tracial joint spectral measure and deriving the Laplace representation (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A finite von Neumann algebra equipped with a faithful normal tracial state and a pair of positive bounded operators.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem assumes finite tracial von Neumann algebras; it does not state the corresponding result for arbitrary or semifinite algebras.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract extends a conjecture known for matrix algebras to a broader operator-algebra setting and the record cross-lists operator algebras, functional analysis, and mathematical physics.

sections.title: Sharpness of the Osgood threshold for anomalous dissipation and non-uniqueness in passive scalar transport
sections.abstract: For every concave non-Osgood modulus, the authors construct a divergence-free velocity field on the two-torus producing anomalous dissipation, establishing sharpness of the Osgood threshold and a related transport non-uniqueness threshold.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that for any concave non-Osgood modulus ω there is u∈L∞([0,1];C^ω(T²)) and smooth initial data producing anomalous dissipation; they derive sharpness of the Osgood condition for uniqueness of bounded transport solutions (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Passive scalar advection-diffusion on T², divergence-free velocity in L∞ time with spatial modulus C^ω, concave non-Osgood ω, and smooth initial data.
sections.unique_caveat: The construction is for the two-dimensional torus and the specified concave non-Osgood moduli; it does not assert the same for every flow or domain.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract resolves a sharp-threshold question uniformly over a whole class of moduli and links anomalous dissipation to transport non-uniqueness.

sections.title: A proof of a conjecture on bipartite correspondence packing
sections.abstract: The author proves a conjecture on full correspondence packings of finite bipartite graphs, with an explicit color-list size asymptotic to D/log D.
sections.claimed_result: For sufficiently large D, every correspondence cover of a finite bipartite graph with maximum cover degree at most D has a full correspondence packing when each vertex has k(D)=ceil(D/(log D−2log log D−6)) colors; the author proves the cited conjecture (arXiv abstract and Theorem 1).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite bipartite graph; correspondence cover degree at most D; the explicit formula is stated for D≥ceil(e^20), with k(D) asymptotic to D/log D.
sections.unique_caveat: The explicit theorem’s stated asymptotic regime begins at the very large threshold D≥ceil(e^20); it is a sufficient condition, not a claim of optimal finite-D constants.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper proves a named 2024 conjecture and provides an explicit asymptotic threshold; it is cross-listed in combinatorics and discrete mathematics.

sections.title: A proof of Schmeisser's conjecture
sections.abstract: The author proves Schmeisser’s strengthening of Sendov’s conjecture in every degree and reports a Lean 4 formalization alongside computer-assisted verification in a finite range.
sections.claimed_result: If a degree-n≥2 polynomial has all zeros in the closed unit disk, then every point in their convex hull lies within distance 1 of a critical point; the author states a proof in every degree (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Complex polynomial of degree n≥2 with all zeros in the closed unit disk; ξ is any point in the convex hull of the zeros.
sections.unique_caveat: The proof includes computer-assisted verification for a finite degree range; the abstract reports a Lean 4 formalization, but this report has not audited that artifact.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: This is the week’s substantive revision: v2 adds a Lean 4 formalization and remarks to an all-degree conjecture proof; the record was revised on 17 November.

sections.title: On Hilbert's tenth problem for number fields
sections.abstract: The authors show conditionally that the integers are Diophantine in number fields, giving a negative answer to Hilbert’s tenth problem under the abc conjecture and a rank condition.
sections.claimed_result: Assuming abc over a number field K and a positive-rank elliptic curve E/Q with rank E(Q)=rank E(K), the authors prove Z is Diophantine in K, hence Hilbert’s tenth problem over K is undecidable; for quadratic K the rank condition is available, leaving abc as the assumption (arXiv abstract and Theorem 1.1).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A number field K; abc over K; and a positive-rank elliptic curve over Q whose rank is unchanged over K. For quadratic K, the paper says such curves always exist.
sections.unique_caveat: The conclusion remains conditional on abc over K; for general K it also requires the stated elliptic-curve rank condition, and concerns the field K rather than its ring of integers.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A direct conditional theorem on Hilbert’s tenth problem across number fields, cross-listed in number theory and logic, with the hypotheses stated explicitly in the abstract.

sections.title: A disproof of the El-Zahar--Erdős conjecture
sections.abstract: The authors disprove the El-Zahar–Erdős conjecture by constructing high-girth graphs of arbitrarily large chromatic number where every pair of disjoint induced subgraphs each needing at least seven colors has an edge between them.
sections.claimed_result: For every integer g≥4 there are graphs of girth at least g and arbitrarily large chromatic number such that any two vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs each of chromatic number at least seven are joined by an edge (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite graphs with prescribed girth lower bound g≥4 and unbounded chromatic number; the separation threshold is chromatic number seven.
sections.unique_caveat: The counterexample is stated at threshold seven; the abstract does not determine the optimal threshold or all lower-threshold variants.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract gives a strong counterexample family simultaneously controlling girth and chromatic number, directly answering a named graph-theoretic conjecture.
